text1: All robins are birds. Pip is a robin. What must be true?
hint: Apply the general rule to Pip.
know_more: If every robin is a bird and Pip is a robin, Pip must be a bird.

text1: Mia is taller than Leo. Who is shorter?
know_more: If Mia is taller, Leo is shorter.

text1: Every square has 4 sides. This shape is a square. How many sides does it have?
know_more: A square has four sides.

text1: If it rains, the playground gets wet. It is raining. What follows?
hint: The condition in the rule has happened.
know_more: Rain implies the playground gets wet.

text1: Nina has 3 red marbles and 2 blue marbles. Does she have more red than blue?
know_more: 3 red is more than 2 blue.

text1: Ben finished before Tara in a race. Who was ahead of the other?
know_more: Ben finished before Tara.

text1: No triangles have 4 sides. This shape has 4 sides. Can it be a triangle?
know_more: A four-sided shape cannot be a triangle.

text1: All library books have labels. This is a library book. What should it have?
hint: Apply the rule to the object.
know_more: Every library book in the statement has a label.

text1: Ava has fewer stickers than Kim. Who has more stickers?
know_more: If Ava has fewer, Kim has more.

text1: If a switch is off, the lamp is dark. The switch is off. What is the lamp like?
know_more: The rule says an off switch makes the lamp dark.

text1: Amy is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Carl. Who is shortest?
know_more: Amy > Ben > Carl in height, so Carl is shortest.

text1: All birds have feathers. Penguins are birds. What must be true about penguins?
hint: Put penguins inside the larger group 'birds'.
know_more: Penguins are birds, and all birds have feathers.

text1: Red box is heavier than blue. Blue is heavier than green. Which is heaviest?
know_more: Red > Blue > Green, so red is heaviest.

text1: No fish are mammals. A dolphin is a mammal. What follows from these statements?
answer: A dolphin is not a fish
option4: A dolphin is not a fish
hint: Use the 'no fish are mammals' rule.
know_more: If no fish are mammals, anything known to be a mammal cannot be a fish.

text1: If homework is complete, Maya may play. Maya's homework is complete. What is supported?
know_more: The given rule permits play when homework is complete.

text1: A, B, and C stand in a line. A is before B and B is before C. Who is in the middle?
know_more: A-B-C places B in the middle.

text1: Every blue card is numbered. Card X is blue. Card X is not numbered. Which statement cannot all be true?
hint: Apply the universal rule to Card X.
know_more: If every blue card is numbered and X is blue, X must be numbered, so saying it is not numbered creates a contradiction.

text1: Lena has more coins than Omar but fewer than Priya. Who has the most?
hint: Place Lena between the other two.
know_more: Priya > Lena > Omar.

text1: If a number is even, it can be divided by 2 with no remainder. 18 is even. What follows?
hint: Use the property of even numbers.
know_more: 18 is even, so 18÷2 leaves no remainder.

text1: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are yellow. Can we conclude all roses are yellow?
hint: Do not transfer a property from 'some flowers' to all roses.
know_more: Knowing some flowers are yellow does not tell us that all roses are yellow.

text1: In a race, Ben finished before Cara. Asha finished after Cara. Dev finished before Ben. Who finished first?
know_more: Dev is before Ben, Ben before Cara, and Cara before Asha: Dev-Ben-Cara-Asha.

text1: Four books P,Q,R,S are stacked. P is above Q. R is below Q. S is above P. Which is on top?
hint: Build the stack from the relations.
know_more: S is above P, which is above Q, which is above R. S is top.

text1: Every Zim is a Tor. No Tor is a Fen. Kiko is a Zim. What must be true?
hint: Move Kiko through the set rules.
know_more: Kiko is a Zim, so Kiko is a Tor. No Tor is a Fen, so Kiko cannot be a Fen.

text1: A box has more red balls than blue, and more blue than green. There are 3 green balls. What is the smallest possible number of red balls?
hint: Use the smallest whole numbers that keep both 'more than' relations true.
know_more: Green=3, so the smallest blue is 4 and smallest red is 5.

text1: Ali, Bea, Chen, and Dina sit in a row. Ali is left of Bea. Chen is right of Bea. Dina is left of Ali. Who is farthest left?
hint: Turn each relation into an order.
know_more: Dina is left of Ali, Ali left of Bea, Bea left of Chen: Dina-Ali-Bea-Chen.

text1: If the library is open, the lights are on. The lights are off. What can we conclude about the library?
hint: If open always means lights on, can open be true while lights are off?
know_more: Given the rule, an open library would have lights on. Since lights are off, it is not open.

text1: Three boxes have labels: Red, Blue, Green. The prize is not in Red and not in Green. Where is it?
know_more: Only Blue remains after excluding Red and Green.

text1: M is older than N. N is older than P. Q is younger than P. Who is definitely youngest?
know_more: M>N>P>Q, so Q is youngest.

text1: A code lock uses one digit from 1,2,3,4. It is greater than 2 and not even. Which digit is it?
know_more: Greater than 2 leaves 3 or 4; not even removes 4, leaving 3.

text1: Four tasks W,X,Y,Z obey: W before X, X before Y, and Z after Y. Which task must be last?
know_more: W→X→Y→Z, so Z must be last.
